q: Crossing two genetically different plants to combine desirable traits is called:
why: Hybridization combines desirable traits of two different parent plants.

q: Inducing useful variation using radiation or chemicals is known as:
why: Mutation breeding deliberately induces mutations using radiation/chemicals.

q: The Green Revolution mainly increased yields of:
why: High-yielding dwarf varieties of wheat and rice drove the Green Revolution.

q: Dwarf wheat varieties were valuable in the Green Revolution mainly because they:
o: Resisted lodging (falling over) and gave higher yield
why: Dwarf stems resist lodging, allowing higher yields to be supported.

q: The scientific management of dairy animals for improved milk production is called:
why: Animal husbandry includes breeding and managing dairy animals for better milk yield.

q: Rearing of domestic fowl for eggs and meat is called:
why: Poultry farming is the practice of raising birds like chickens for eggs and meat.

q: Single Cell Protein (SCP) refers to protein-rich biomass obtained mainly from:
why: SCP is protein derived from cultured microorganisms, used as a food/feed supplement.

q: Tissue culture technique used to produce many identical plantlets from a small plant part is called:
why: Micropropagation (tissue culture) multiplies plants rapidly from small tissue explants.

q: Choosing naturally superior plants from an existing population and propagating them is called:
why: Selection is picking already superior plants rather than creating new combinations.

q: A key advantage of micropropagation over seed propagation is:
o: It produces genetically identical disease-free plants quickly
why: Micropropagation rapidly multiplies genetically uniform, disease-free plantlets.
